messages:
Anya: Quick sync on kernel + KV sprint status — can owners call out blockers and any dependency timing? We need to align for the next canary deploy (goal: Thurs). Owners I have: @Matt (kernel), @Raj (continuous-batching), @Oliver (KV cache).

Matt: Kernel PR #1347 is in review, tests mostly green but failing on fp16 path in our internal perf harness. I pinged @Jen for infra repro. ETA for a fix attempt EOD Tue.

Raj: Batch perf tests show ~2.3x throughput win at seq=512, but p99 latency spikes under bursty short requests. Investigating handshake/backpressure between batcher and kernel. Might need a small backoff.

Oliver: KV eviction bug is a race between prefetcher and async GC. I have a branch (kv-locks) that adds a narrow lock around the prefetch table; fixes correctness but drops throughput ~5% on microbenchmarks.

Jen: I can repro the KV race in staging with a synthetic workload. Suggest we can canary the lock fix behind a feature flag on dedicated capacity before full rollout.

Anya: Can we get concise numbers to decide? @Matt can you run the kernel PR + kv-lock branch end-to-end and post token/sec + p99? If the tradeoff is small, prefer correctness then explore lock-free options.

Matt: Ran a quick end-to-end with kernel PR + kv-lock on a 4xA100 staging pool: token/sec down ~4%, p99 improved 420ms -> 380ms. Short log snippet: ```
# perf summary
tokens/sec: 1240 -> 1190
p50: 60ms -> 58ms
p99: 420ms -> 380ms
```

Raj: Thanks. If kernel changes remove some micro-optimizations we might see another few percent. Proposal for rollout sequence: 1) merge non-breaking kernel fixes, 2) canary KV-lock on dedicated with feature flag for 24h, 3) enable adjusted batching config gradually and monitor p95/p99.

Anya: Sounds reasonable. Need explicit ownership and PRs to watch: @Matt will own kernel PR #1347, @Oliver will own kv-lock branch PR #1359, @Raj will own the batching config PR #1362. @Sophia can you review #1362 for config safety? @Jen will run the staging canary + traces.

Sophia: +1, can review #1362 tomorrow morning.

Oliver: One open question — do we accept the ~5% throughput hit temporarily? If so, I'll push the lock fix behind a flag so we can toggle it quickly.

Anya: Let's do the feature-flagged canary. If p99 improves and user-visible errors drop, we keep it and iterate on lock-free approach. Action items: Matt: fix fp16 failure (EOD Tue). Oliver: open PR with flag + perf numbers (today). Raj: add p99 dashboards and a small synthetic test to reproduce tail. Jen: schedule canary and collect traces. Sophia: review config PR. I'll own rollout coordination and stakeholder comms.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot scheduled canary: dedicated-capacity/us-west2 -> 2026-03-18 02:00 UTC (feature-flag: kv-locks).

Anya: Thanks everyone — post updates in this thread as you have them. If anything slips, call it out and we'll re-prioritize. :thumbsup:
